# II. Auxiliary Functions

In this section, we design some general-use functions which may find place in subroutines used in the building of more complex functions: - sums / higher moments - exponentiation - square root - log

We will also be using these functions as examples to show **techniques** that would be useful in other scenarios. Specifically: 

1. Exponentiation shows the power of **Taylor series**. 

2. The square root conveys the utility of **giving computation back to the user post-FHE**.

## Some Basics

We are allowed to generate encoded vectors of any constant, c. $$ct_c=enc(c_1, c_2, \dots,c_{N/2})$$ Note that $c_i$ can be distinct from $c_j$ This allows us to do computations with pre-computed constant vectors $$c*enc(z_*)=enc(c,c,\dots,c)*enc(z_*)=enc(cz_1,cz_2,\dots,cz_{N/2})$$ Naturally, this allows us to do operations on unencrypted data and apply them to our encrypted data like taking the inverse of c: $$ct_{*}=enc(\frac{1}{c},\frac{1}{c},\dots,\frac{1}{c})$$

### Selection Vector (a.k.a. One-Hot, Masking, Binary Vector)

Suppose we want certain elements in our ciphertext. We can encrypt a vector of ones (selected) and zeros (not selected) to decide on which elements are needed. For example, if we wanted to take only the first element of our vector $ct=enc(z_1,z_2,\dots z_{N/2})$, all we need is one multiplication with our pre-encrypted $ct_0=enc(1,0,0,\dots0)$ to obtain $$ct_*=ct_0*ct=enc(1,0,0,\dots,0)*enc(z_1,z_2,\dots, z_{N/2})=enc(z_1,0,0,\dots,0)$$
